svg.title: Within-class spread only hurts along the separating direction
svg.desc: Three scatter panels, each with two class clouds whose centroids sit at the same two points joined by a horizontal line. Panel A has tight round clouds and the highest H-score. Panel B has wide round clouds and a visibly lower score. Panel C has clouds stretched vertically, across the horizontal direction separating the centroids, and carries exactly the same total within-class variance as B, yet its score returns to panel A's value.
svg.text: The centroids never move. Only the within-class spread changes.
B and C carry exactly the same total within-class variance, yet C scores as well as A.
What costs you is spread along the separating direction — not spread as such.
